VILLACORTA DILG Region 58 McArthur Highway Matina, Davao City Dear Director Villacorta: This refers to your 27 Februar. 2015 Mem randum requesting the Central Office's clarification, as follows: "May activities such as conduct of easibility studies, project development studies and other pre-implemeniation acti ities in connection (l'itll development ro•ects listed in DILG-DBM oint Memor ndum Circular No. 2011-1 be funded by the Local Development Fund?" It is the position of the Regional Office that the conduct of feasibility studies, project development studies and other pre-implementati n activities may be charged to the 20% Local Development Fund. Soft projects or activities s ch as conduct of feasibility studies, project development studies and other pre-implementati n activities relate to a developmental project included in the list of projects enumerated under DILG-DBM JMC No. 2011-1 as supported by DILG Opinion No. 14, s. 2011, dated 06 May 201 In response to the above query, please find belo the following discussions relative thereto: Nature of the 20% Local Development Fund Section 287 of the Local Government Code (RA 7160) requires each local government unit to appropriate in its annual budget no less than enty percent (20%) of its annual internal revenue allotment (IRA) for developm€pt proje ts, viz:

"Section 287. Lacal Developntent rojects. - Each local governillent unit shall appropriate in its annual budget n less than tzventy percent (20%) of its annual internal revenue allotment for development projects. Copies of the development plané of local government un •ts shall be furnished the Department of Interior aud Local Governwent." [Unders oring ours] "Local Development," as explained in the DILG- LGS Source Book entitled, Rationalizing the Local Planning Systemi, pertains to the mand tes and responsibilities of local government units as defined in Sections 16 and 17 of RA 71 . Funds for local development is not limited to the 20% of the IRA allotted for developmen projects (hereinafter, "LDF") because LGUs spend more on "development" than the LDF. The LDF, as broadly defined, is that portion of e local budget that is "plowed back" to the people in the form of programs, projects, and ervices as opposed to that portion which is consumed by the local government machinery ( alaries and wages and other personnel costs, office maintenance and other operating expendi es, and office capital outlay).2 Hence, office expenses, office MOOE, and offic capital outlay are excluded from the LDF as the same are not treated as investment on devel pment. Note however that the LGU's budget for devel pment projects/p!ograms/activities (PPAs) is not limited to the 20% LDF as tlme latter only present a portion of the total budget that is reflected as one of the sources for financing PP s contained in the Annual Investment Plan (AIP). Mav Pre-lmplementation Activities be Charged Against (he 20% Local Development Fund? It is this level's opinion that pre-implementation ctivities may not be charged against the 20% local development fund notwithstanding the fact that said activities are conducted in connection with a developmental project identi ed under DILG-DBM JMC No. 2011-1. The appropriations for development projects n from the 20% local development fund are investments on development and should be utili ed solely for said purpose. Hence, incidental expenses in relation to the implementation of sa• projects should be taken from other sources considering that the 200/6 local development only represents a slice of the LGU's budget for development (note the above discussion on e nature of the 20% local development fund). 1" Edition, 2008, Published by the DILG-BLGD Page 165, ibid.

Further, DILG Opinion No. 14, s. 2011 cannot e applied herein considering that the subject of said opinion, i.e., "soft infrastructure proje ', refers to the developmental project of the LGU therein and is not an incidental expense in connection with the implementation of a developmental project, as in the case herein. N e however that DILG Opinion No, 14, s. 2011 is not conclusive on the subject as the Central Office has requested the DBM's guidance/definitive opinion on whether the u • •zation of the 20% local development fund is limited to capital expenditures. Hence, pendin receipt of the DBM's response to our query, the Region is advised to refrain from making a y further reference to DILG Opinion No. 14, s. 2011. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A.
